risks: No participants are involved; the risk is a misleading summary that drives a costly lease or rejects a useful one.
consent: Not applicable: only published and publicly reported data are used.
data: No personal data; the search strategy, screening log, extraction form and analysis code are archived with the report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: age over 75, rural residence with poor mobile coverage, living alone, lower income and not owning a smartphone may reduce access and benefit. The review extracts results for these groups where reported and names trials that excluded them, so the committee can weigh loaned phones, offline devices or clinic synchronisation.
effectiveness: The review succeeds if the committee can see the size and certainty of any effect on function and adherence before deciding.
efficiency: Uses existing library and physiotherapy time; no new data collection.
costs: Staff time within existing roles (20 information specialist hours and about 16 physiotherapist days).
partnerships: Library service, procurement committee, two patient partners from the joint replacement class, and the centre's digital services team for coverage questions.
rebPath: No research ethics review is required for a review of published data; the report goes to the procurement committee, and any later local evaluation of the devices would be screened separately.
limitations: Shortcuts (single screening with a 20 percent check, English only, no author contact) may miss evidence; results may not transfer to rural patients with poor coverage.
summary: Low-risk review of published data with an explicit equity lens on age, rurality and technology access.
